title: VPC capacity + BOM quick-sizer (private deployments)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, conservative sizing worksheet + BOM checklist for Private / VPC Redwood deployments. Meant to convert a customer workload profile into a ~90-day steady-state GPU fleet proposal plus recommended components for a single-region on-prem or cloud VPC install. 

Notes / audience:
- Working doc: early sales and infra-eng reference. Use for SOW + initial procurement estimate.
- Not a final quote: network design, rack space, power feed, and procurement discounts will change numbers.
- Assumptions are explicit below; change them per-customer.

Top-level assumptions (editable):
- target_p99_latency_ms = 200 (for generation requests unless otherwise stated)
- target_utilization_percent = 70 (target average GPU occupancy to leave headroom)
- model_profile = gpt-medium (approx 20B, KV cache behavior typical)
- tokens_per_request_avg = 120 (input+output tokens)
- requests_per_minute_peak = 6000 (concurrent QPS equivalent: 100 rps)
- sustained_hours_per_day = 24
- expected_daily_traffic_growth = 0.05 (5% monthly)
- on-node_inference_throughput_tokens_per_sec_per_gpu = 9000 (baseline for A100-80GB equivalent using Redwood runtime and quantization profile)
calculation_steps:
1) Convert customer traffic to tokens/sec:
   tokens_per_sec_peak = requests_per_minute_peak / 60 * tokens_per_request_avg
   Example: 6000 / 60 * 120 = 12,000 tps

2) GPU raw capacity (tokens/sec) = on-node_inference_throughput_tokens_per_sec_per_gpu * efficiency_factor
   efficiency_factor = target_utilization_percent / 100
   Effective_tokens_per_gpu = 9000 * 0.70 = 6300 tps

3) Required GPUs = ceil(tokens_per_sec_peak / Effective_tokens_per_gpu)
   Example: 12,000 / 6,300 = 1.90 => 2 GPUs (BUT add redundancy and warm-headroom)

4) Redundancy / HA policy: we recommend N+1 within region for mission-critical (i.e., add 1 spare server per cluster)
   - For small counts (<=8 GPUs) prefer 1 spare host; larger fleets use 10% spare capacity rounded up.

5) Burst capacity: if peak bursts exceed baseline by >25%, add burst pooling or scale-in window.

6) Rack / host mapping: choose server GPU count that matches model memory + throughput: e.g., 4x A100-80GB per 1RU server or 8x A10/A30 per 2RU chassis. Adjust per customer footprint.

7) Example end-to-end for example profile:
   - tokens_per_sec_peak = 12,000
   - Effective_tokens_per_gpu = 6,300
   - Required GPUs = 2 -> but with N+1 => 3 GPUs total
   - If using 4x-GPU hosts -> requires 1 host (4 GPUs) but recommend 2 hosts to allow rolling upgrades AND rack diversity -> Proposed fleet = 2 hosts x 4 GPUs = 8 GPUs total (oversized for HA and growth)

BOM & components checklist (single region baseline):
- Compute hosts:
  - Option A: 1RU - 4x A100-80GB, 2x 2TB NVMe boot, 1x 100G RDMA NIC, redundant PSUs, 512 GB system RAM (part #: RWF-1RU-A100x4)
  - Option B: 2RU - 8x A10/A30 (cost-sensitive), 4 TB NVMe, 2x 100G NICs (part #: RWF-2RU-A10x8)
- Management hosts: 2x small servers for customer-managed control plane (db + api cache), 32GB RAM, 2x 1TB NVMe
- Network: 2x top-of-rack 100G switches (spare port density), 1x aggregation with BGP/ECMP recommended, firewall appliance or cloud VPC routing config
- Storage: 100 TB object store (S3-compatible) + 10 TB for model cache on fast NVMe per region
- Key management: HSM/KMS appliance integration notes (customer managed)
- Power & cooling: per-host PDU capacity estimate (6000W per 1RU A100x4 heavy configs). Verify data center feed
- Licensing & support: 3-year support SKUs, extended warranty, remote hands as-needed

Cost estimate template (unit placeholders—replace with vendor quotes):
- A100x4 host list price = $120k (example) -> per-GPU = $30k
- A10x8 host list price = $75k -> per-GPU = $9.4k
- 100G ToR switch = $25k each
- 100 TB object store (on-prem VMware-scale) = $40k CAPEX equivalent
- HSM integration & KMS annual = $12k

Operational sizing knobs / cautions:
- Model memory pressure: if model requires >30GB VRAM, drop GPUs-per-host or choose 80GB variants. This changes host choice dramatically.
- KV cache hit-rate: with high prefix reuse, effective throughput per GPU increases; rerun with hit rate multiplier (e.g., 1.25x)
- Autoscaling warmup: cold-start/offline nodes add latency. For strict p99 targets, maintain minimum warm pool = 20% of fleet.
- Inter-region replication: if cross-region failover required, plan for dual-active capacity or rapid provisioning runway (cold copies + image bake time).

Single-region sample proposals (conservative / balanced / aggressive):
- Conservative (HA-first): Min fleet = capacity + N+1 + 20% warm = round_up(required_gpus * 1.3) -> example: 2 * 1.3 = 2.6 -> 3 GPUs -> map to 1 host with 4 GPUs -> propose 2 hosts for HA -> total 8 GPUs
- Balanced (growth-aware): required_gpus * 2 (to allow rolling updates) -> propose 4 GPUs -> 1 host if 4x per host -> but still recommend 2 hosts for physical redundancy
- Aggressive (cost-optimized): pack to host capacity, rely on quick auto-scale + burst credits -> propose exact required_gpus + 10%

Delivery checklist (what infra-eng needs to finalize):
- Confirm model memory requirements and quantization profile (contact applied-ml).
- Network egress patterns: will customer stream results externally? need bandwidth calc.
- Storage: retention policy for model artifacts and logs.
- Rack/PDU constraints, power per RU from data center.
- Procurement lead times and preferred vendors.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm whether customer requires HIPAA/PCI FIPS level HSM (affects KMS BOM).
- Get concrete traffic shape (hour-by-hour) to replace peak simplification.
- Run microbenchmark with target model on target hardware; update on-node throughputs.

Appendix: quick formulas to copy into spreadsheet:
- tokens_per_sec_peak = (requests_per_minute_peak / 60) * tokens_per_request_avg
- effective_tokens_per_gpu = on_node_inference_throughput_tokens_per_sec_per_gpu * (target_utilization_percent / 100)
- required_gpus_raw = tokens_per_sec_peak / effective_tokens_per_gpu
- required_gpus_ha = ceil(required_gpus_raw * (1 + spare_fraction)) (spare_fraction typically 0.1 or 0.33 for N+1 small)

Slack refs / tickets: see linked_artifacts at top for continuity.

Version notes: 2026-02-10: switched default throughput to Redwood runtime v2.1 benchmarks; split BOM into Option A (high-performance) and Option B (cost sensitive).

Quick usage guide for sales engineer: paste customer inputs at top, run steps 1-3, then translate required GPU count into host count using chosen host config; add redundancy per policy; factor procurement lead time into rollout schedule.

End of sheet.
